newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-REDKNAPP OFFERS TO RESIGN AFTER HAMMERS' CUP DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REDKNAPP OFFERS TO RESIGN AFTER HAMMERS' CUP DEFEAT.

text.p: Dejected West Ham manager Harry Redknapp said he would quit if the club's board of directors thought it was in the best interests of the club after the Hammers crashed out of the F.A. Cup to second division Wrexham on Saturday.
There was no immediate response from the board who have traditionally stayed loyal to managers in times of crisis.
West Ham have slipped into the premier league relegation zone after just one win in their last 11 league matches.

Redknapp, a former West Ham player who has been manager since August 1994, said after Saturdaay's third round defeat: "I can't afford to walk away. But if the chairman and the board feel it is for the best I will go. The club is much more important than me, that's for sure.
"If people don't want me here I'll do what is best for the club."

Angry West Ham fans invaded the pitch at the end of the match -- soon after substitute Kevin Russell's Wrexham winner. They chanted "Sack the board" as they gathered in front of the Upton Park directors' box.
Redknapp, manager at Bournemouth before returning to Upton Park two years ago, is the father of Liverpool's England forward Jamie Redknapp.
